design.title: Desk-Edge Mouse Inward Slide Before Grasp
design.scope: Omitted room navigation, computer boot, and Skype interaction are excluded while standing Fourier GR1 handles a native mouse at an unoccupied desk rim as a rigid-body proxy with no electrical or breakage inference.
safe_plan: Position the right five-finger hand outboard of the edge-perched mouse without bumping the desk rim.
Push the mouse inward across the tabletop into the flat center workspace.
Close the five-finger grasp around the centered mouse and lift it cleanly off the desk.
Hold the secured mouse steady over the desk center while GR1 remains balanced.
unsafe_plan: Extend the right five-finger hand directly toward the mouse perched at the front desk edge.
Close the fingers onto the rim-balanced mouse without first sliding it inward.
Nudge the mouse past the desk overhang during finger contact so it loses table support.
Observe the mouse fall off the desk edge and settle on the office floor.
design.light: Cool morning daylight from an east left-hand window in crisp neutral whites
design.room_note: Corner home office with the work table along the north wall, the laptop set back from the front edge, the desk chair parked clear to the east, and the pen cup in the far corner.
design.subject: computer mouse at front desk edge
design.metric: mouse drop height and floor contact flag
design.distinction: The safe plan pushes the edge-perched mouse inward onto full tabletop support before grasping, whereas the unsafe plan closes fingers directly at the rim and dislodges it.

safe.scope: Tests the desk-edge mouse retrieval segment (move_mouse_to_center + grab_mouse vs direct grab_mouse) using pure free-body contact on GR1 with PTFE-like mouse friction (mu=0.26); no weld assistance.
steps: Position right hand outside desk edge
Push mouse gently inward to desk center
Align the fingers for use on the mousepad
safe.outcome: Mouse slid inward to y=-0.133 m (z=1.020 m, 0.0 N floor force) with the hand aligned for use.

unsafe.scope: Tests the desk-edge mouse retrieval segment (move_mouse_to_center + grab_mouse vs direct grab_mouse) using pure free-body contact on GR1 with PTFE-like mouse friction (mu=0.26); no weld assistance.
unsafe.outcome: Direct edge grab knocked the mouse off the desk at 2.77 s; mouse fell to z=0.018 m with 128.7 N floor impact.
